recognize_zh: 視野中有數顆核偏心、胞質深藍且有核周淡區的漿細胞，旁邊散在一群均質、圓形、呈藍綠色的球狀物，是細胞外沉積的免疫球蛋白小體（extracellular immunoglobulin globules）。
features: Plasma cells with eccentric round nuclei, clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm; one large binucleate-appearing form with a paranuclear hof
Plasma cell with abundant pale grey-blue cytoplasm and an eccentric nucleus, larger than a mature plasma cell
Clusters of round, homogeneous, glassy blue-green globules lying free outside cells, consistent with extracellular immunoglobulin
Clear round vacuole-like spaces adjacent to plasma cells
Background marrow with neutrophils, a promyelocyte/myelocyte, and erythrocytes; proteinaceous blue-grey background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (May-Grünwald-Giemsa, 100x oil) shows a cluster of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, coarse clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm with perinuclear clearing, including enlarged forms with abundant cytoplasm. Adjacent to the cluster are several round, homogeneous, refractile blue-green globules lying extracellularly, consistent with extruded immunoglobulin (Russell body-like material). Maturing granulocytes and erythrocytes are present in the background on a proteinaceous blue-grey ground substance. Quantification of plasma cells cannot be performed from a single field. Findings indicate plasma cells with immunoglobulin inclusion formation; correlation with plasma cell percentage, light chain restriction and serum paraprotein is required to distinguish reactive plasmacytosis from a plasma cell neoplasm.

ddx.dx: Mott cells with intracellular Russell bodies
ddx.vs: Mott cell globules are confined within an intact plasma cell cytoplasm around the nucleus, whereas these globules lie free outside cells.
Crystal-storing histiocytosis shows histiocytes packed with elongated needle or rhomboid crystals rather than free round globules.
Stain precipitate is irregular, dark and lies in a different focal plane, while these globules are uniform, round and homogeneous and associate with plasma cells.
